title: The 100 the City pays most: who has almost no private grants
question: Which of the largest City-funded nonprofits draw little or nothing from private foundations?
finding: Of the 100 nonprofits the City pays most, 6 received no grant at all from the 3,246 grantmakers on file in 2020 to 2025, and for 22 private grants were under 1% of City and private money combined; the City paid those 22 organizations $1.86 billion in fiscal 2020 to 2025. The largest with none: Richmond Area Multi-Services Inc ($163.1 million), Baker Places Inc ($109.9 million), The Yerba Buena Gardens Conservancy ($52.9 million), Providence Foundation of San Francisco ($38.3 million). The middle organization of the 100 drew 4.8% of the combined total from these funders.
how: The 100 nonprofits with the largest City payments in fiscal 2019 to 2026 were taken from the City's nonprofit spending file. For each, every grant PAID to it was added up from the tax returns of 3,246 Bay Area private foundations, large California foundations and community foundations, by the calendar year in which the funder's tax period ends (2020 to 2025; 2025 is incomplete). A grant counts when the funder's return prints the organization's federal employer number, or prints its exact name with an address in San Francisco or in a city the organization files its own return from. City money is City fiscal years 2020 to 2025. The share is private grants divided by private grants plus City payments. The later columns come from the organization's own tax return (Form 990): contributions other than government grants, and City payments divided by total revenue, over the return years on file. Matching: 17,504 grant rows were taken to be City-paid organizations, 3,430 of them on an employer number and the rest on name and address (639 of those on a one-word name, kept only with a matching address and labelled). Set aside and in no total: 969 rows ($47.1 million) where the same name is printed with an address in another city, 15 one-word names with no matching address, and $1.57 billion to universities, public bodies and organizations the City paid less than $750,000. Rows with a negative or blank amount are left out.
limits: The funders on file are Bay Area and large California grantmakers only: national foundations, the national donor-advised-fund sponsors, companies and individual donors are not in it, so 'private grants found' is a floor, and the organization's own return (the columns after the years) is the better guide to its whole private income. A fiscal sponsor receives grants for the projects it hosts. Hospitals and national bodies file one return for work far beyond San Francisco, which makes the City's share of their revenue look small. Matching by name can miss a grant printed under another name and can pick up a namesake; grants to a same-named organization in another city were set aside. State and federal funding of the same organizations is in the State grants and federal money screens (linked in the last column), and City payments tested against reported revenue are in the 'Do the books agree?' screens; neither is repeated here.
